A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DeGF research and contain 31 readable pages, including Appendices A–E. Text, equations, tables, and rendered figures support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark experiments, generative-feedback analyses, ablations, efficiency measurements, and qualitative evaluations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 1–7, Tables C1–C14, and the appendix case studies.

M1.justification: Visual-reference generation, JS-divergence-based selection between complementary and contrastive decoding, and adaptive plausibility constraints remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix B.

E1.justification: Both evaluate POPE using MS-COCO, A-OKVQA, and GQA, alongside CHAIR, MME-Hallucination, MMBench, MMVP, and LLaVA-Bench. MMVet evaluation is already present in Appendix C.4 of v1 and remains in v2.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding experiments, including Regular, VCD, M3ID, RITUAL, and the experiment-specific Woodpecker, HALC, DoLa, and OPERA comparisons. Correcting Woodpecker's citation does not change the evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The model backbones and sizes, sample counts, CHAIR token limits, sampling and greedy-decoding conditions, prompts, and evaluation metrics are retained. Removing the Experimental Settings subsection heading does not remove or revise its settings.

E4.justification: Both retain the threshold and generative-model ablations, hyperparameter sensitivity analyses, model-scaling evaluation, acceleration studies, generated-image quality assessment, and success/failure case studies in the main text and appendices.

E5.justification: Both report MME means and standard deviations across three random seeds in Section 4, Table 3, and Table C3. No run counts, uncertainty-reporting practices, or statistical tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: All tabulated values, plotted outcomes, and case-study results are unchanged. However, the POPE paragraph broadens its reported best-accuracy ranking from two LVLMs across 18 settings to three LVLMs across all settings. The retained Table 1 does not support that extension: Qwen-VL on MS-COCO random sampling scores 89.73 for DeGF versus 89.83 for M3ID in both PDFs.

T1.justification: Equations 1–10, including the JS-divergence definition, decoding rules, metric formulas, and plausibility constraint, are unchanged. Neither version adds formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same training-free DeGF contribution, generative-feedback novelty claim, and claimed hallucination-mitigation effectiveness across six benchmarks.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations, interpretations of generative feedback, computational and real-time limitations in Appendix A, and interpretations of success and failure cases in Appendix D remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The code-access information, implementation defaults, GPU specification, prompts, diffusion-step settings, baseline implementation details, and dataset/code licenses are retained. The added author contact information does not change code or data access.

R1.justification: The cited-work set and research positioning remain unchanged. Woodpecker's attribution is corrected to the already-cited Yin et al. (2023), and the Reflective Instruction Tuning reference receives bibliographic updates; neither introduces new related work.

P1.justification: v2 removes the Experimental Settings heading and renumbers subsequent Section 4 subsections, shortens the ethics statement, and updates affiliations, contact information, acknowledgements, and citation details. The overall narrative and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 3's caption now correctly describes binned CHAIR_I bars and specifies CLIP similarity scaling by 100; the graphic itself is unchanged. Table 1 spacing and some page flow change slightly, with no figures or tables added or removed.

improvement.justification: The Figure 3 caption and Woodpecker citation corrections improve local accuracy. However, v2 expands the supported POPE accuracy claim from 18 settings on two models to all settings on three, although unchanged Table 1 shows DeGF below a comparator in five Qwen-VL settings. This unsupported generalization outweighs the small editorial corrections in results-reporting accuracy; the unchanged methods, experiments, and appendices limit the decline.
